programme.desc: S3 E10 — What Lies Below?More than 80 per cent of the Earth's oceans remain unexplored, and in many ways, the underwater world is the host's 'final frontier'. As new technology allows people to explore oceans and deep lakes more than ever before, nobody knows what they will find.

programme.title: World's Most Unexplained
programme.desc: S1 E13 — Celtic CreaturesAccording to folklore, pots of gold and wishes are granted if a Leprechaun is caught. These mysterious little creatures are seemingly only found in Ireland. Experts debate whether these Celtic creatures are fact or fiction.

programme.title: World's Most Unexplained
programme.desc: S1 E14 — JFK PredictionThe mysterious phone call from an apparently middle-aged woman who predicted the murder of President John F Kennedy. On November 22 1963, a telephone operator in California answered a call that stated that the President was going to die. This came some hours before Lee Harvey Oswald unleashed his fire.

programme.title: World's Most Unexplained
programme.desc: S1 E17 — ApparitionsGod moves in mysterious ways and sometimes appears in mysterious places. This episode lools at claims of mysterious religious sightings. Why do so many people see a vision of Jesus Christ in seemingly normal sights such as a tree stump or an antique cabinet.

programme.title: World's Most Unexplained
programme.desc: S1 E18 — The Truth about PsychicsParanormal experts and skeptics explore the mysterious world of psychics. Is it a talent, a supernatural gift or a hoax.

programme.title: The Proof Is Out There
programme.desc: S3 E9 — Panama UFO Disc, Bloody Red Sea and the Dyatlov Pass IncidentAn examination of several seemingly impossible things 'caught on film', including a flying saucer-shaped object spotted near the Panama Canal and a 'bloody' Red Sea in Egypt. Plus, claims a group of hikers were brutally killed by a Yeti in the mountains of Russia.

programme.title: The Proof Is Out There
programme.desc: S3 E10 — Crocodile Monster, Tiktok USO and Ghost Dog Collar RemovalThe team investigates legendary man-eating croc Gustav, glowing lights in Mexico and chilling footage of a pair of dogs acting like they have just seen a ghost.

programme.title: What on Earth?
programme.desc: S3 E5 — Mystery in the OutbackInvestigators find a new clue about the missing Malaysia Airlines flight that disappeared in 2014. An astronaut spots something strange in the Sahara Desert, and a mysterious orange sludge invades a remote village in Alaska.

programme.title: What on Earth?
programme.desc: S3 E6 — Gateway to EdenA buried monument offers new evidence about one of the Bible's greatest mysteries. An ominous shadow engulfs the Pacific Ocean and scientists have trouble explaining a strange lake that's shaped like a perfect circle.

programme.title: What on Earth?
programme.desc: S3 E7 — The Swastika ConspiracyA dagger sealed in King Tut's tomb for over 3,000 years is made of a possibly extraterrestrial metal. A huge swastika is found in the desert near Roswell.

programme.title: Secrets of the Lost Liners
programme.desc: S2 E3 — Achille LauroA ship with incredible misfortune, the MS Achille Lauro suffered two serious collisions, multiple onboard fires and was even hijacked by PLO terrorists in 1985.

programme.title: Secrets of the Lost Liners
programme.desc: S2 E4 — OceanosDocumentary charting the fate of the MTS Oceanos, a French-built and Greek-owned cruise ship that sank off the coast of South Africa in 1991 after suffering uncontrolled flooding to its engine room.

programme.title: Hazardous History with Henry Winkler

programme.title: Hitler's Handmaidens
programme.desc: S1 E2 — Nazi She-DevilThe Second World War unleashed the full horror of the Nazis on Poland, the Baltic States, Ukraine and Russia. Approximately 500,000 German women served on the Eastern front and the settlement of conquered lands commenced. The colonisers' death camps were established with support by secretaries, administrators, SS wives and female concentration camp guards. This episode explores how women were active participants and perpetrators in the war and its attendant atrocities - especially the Holocaust.

programme.title: Hitler's Secret Sex Life
programme.desc: S1 E2 — Body ImageThe myriad of rumours, theories and disputed historical accounts of Adolf Hitler's sexual psychology, considering how it integrated into his overall twisted psyche. This series addresses various time periods of Hitler's alleged and proven sex life and explores the role sex played in shaping Hitler's behaviour.

programme.title: Weird Britain

programme.title: Weird Britain

He retraces the steps of notorious serial killers Burke and Hare, explores the story of Felicity the puma, the only big cat ever captured in Britain, and discovers the decaying remains of the trap that once captured her, hidden in an overgrown forest. Later, he travels to the battlefield of Culloden to highlight how this significant battle profoundly impacted Scotland's future before heading to Lochs Morar and Ness to test his remote submersible in the depths of these infamous monster lakes.

programme.title: History's Greatest Mysteries
programme.desc: S4 E19 — Unlocking the Secrets of the Nazca LinesLaurence Fishburne explores the Nazca Lines. Dubbed 'the world's greatest archaeological enigma' these 2,000-year-old geoglyphs span over 50 miles of the Peruvian desert. The drawings are so massive they can only be seen from the air. Fishburne contemplates whether new research might finally unravel their secrets.

programme.title: Medieval Murder Mysteries
programme.desc: S1 E2 — King Edward II: A Mysterious DeathIn England, 1327, the body of the recently disposed king Edward II lays on his cell at Berkeley Castle, waiting to be embalmed. If official accounts are to be believed, Edward died from natural causes while in custody after his forced abdication. For some, the demise of the former king was suspiciously timely and all too convenient for his enemies.

programme.title: What on Earth?

programme.title: World's Most Unexplained
programme.desc: S1 E13 — Celtic CreaturesAccording to folklore, pots of gold and wishes are granted if a Leprechaun is caught. These mysterious little creatures are seemingly only found in Ireland. Alleged sightings of leprechauns and fairies are nothing new in Ireland. In fact, many claim they are part of everyday life on the Emerald Isle. Experts debate whether these Celtic creatures are fact or fiction.

programme.title: World's Most Unexplained
programme.desc: S1 E14 — JFK PredictionThe mysterious phone call from an apparently middle-aged woman who predicted the murder of President John F Kennedy. On November 22 1963, a telephone operator in California answered a call that stated that the President was going to die. This came some hours before Lee Harvey Oswald unleashed his fire.

programme.title: Discovered by Disaster
programme.desc: S1 E2 — Cataclysms and SecretsUnexpected things revealed by catastrophic disasters, featuring explorations of Seahenge's 4,000-year-old Bronze Age timber circle, an unusual Ukrainian canoe, ancient remains in a mudslide and a relic from Lake Mead's dry bed.

programme.title: Britain's Most Historic Towns
programme.desc: S2 E6 — Stewart StirlingProfessor Alice Roberts explores the story of Stewart Britain by visiting Stirling, the seat of the Scottish royal family for 200 years. She joins a team of archaeologists in uncovering remnants of the docks, explores the secret passageways of Stirling Castle, learns how to make medieval ale, and discovers the origins of football.

programme.title: Walking Through History
programme.desc: S1 E2 — Frontline DorsetTony Robinson embarks on an expedition along Dorset's Jurassic coast to explore the county's hidden Second World War story. Starting beside the defences on Chesil Beach, he heads east to finish in Swanage and Studland Bay. On his five-day walk he encounters stunning scenery and uncovers wartime acts of ingenuity and bravery. He also discovers the crucial part a swannery played in developing a secret weapon and reveals the role of Dorset in protecting Britain from invasion during the conflict.

programme.desc: A spaceship crash results in the infestation of a small town by aliens, so a Predator is despatched to hunt them down - and any superfluous humans who happen to get in the way. programme.title: The Grand Budapest Hotel
programme.desc: An old man tells a journalist the story of his youth as a lobby boy at a hotel in Eastern Europe in the 1930s. He was taken under the wing of the establishment's dashing concierge, and is drawn into his misadventures as he becomes involved in a conflict over a valuable painting. Wes Anderson's comedy drama, starring Ralph Fiennes, Tony Revolori, F Murray Abraham and Jude Law.

programme.title: Piglet's Big Movie

Animation, featuring the voices of John Fiedler, Jim Cummings and Andre Stojka.

programme.title: Myth: A Frozen Tale
programme.desc: A family sits down for a bedtime story and is transported to a forest filled with elemental spirits. Animated short.

programme.title: The Aristocats
programme.desc: A jealous butler is outraged when his employer leaves a vast fortune to her cat and kittens instead of to him, so he drives the pets to the French countryside and dumps them. However, a streetwise alley cat steps in to help the pampered felines find their way home and claim their rightful inheritance. Animated adventure, with the voices of Eva Gabor, Phil Harris and Scatman Crothers.

programme.title: The Wild
programme.desc: The son of a lion kept in a zoo in Central Park is crated up and shipped to Africa. His worried father musters a band of fellow creatures and escapes from captivity in a quest to rescue the youngster. Animated comedy, featuring the voices of Kiefer Sutherland, James Belushi, Eddie Izzard, Janeane Garofalo and William Shatner.

programme.title: Frozen
programme.desc: A princess with the power to freeze anything she touches loses control of her abilities and plunges the kingdom into a perpetual winter. She goes into hiding, but her sister remains determined that she can be saved from her own magic and sets off on a quest to find her, aided by a mountain man and a living snowman. Disney animated fantasy adventure, with the voices of Kristen Bell and Idina Menzel.

programme.title: Big Hero 6
programme.desc: A lonely, orphaned computer genius forms a special bond with an inflatable robot. When a devastating event occurs in their futuristic home city, they join forces with a group of friends to form a hi-tech band of heroes who are determined to get to the bottom of the matter. Animated adventure, featuring the voices of Ryan Potter, Scott Adsit and Daniel Henney.

programme.title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid
programme.desc: Greg Heffley dreams of becoming famous while trying to survive middle school with his best friend, Rowley. Animated adventure, featuring the voices of Brady Noon, Ethan William Childress and Chris Diamantopoulos.

programme.title: Monsters, Inc
programme.desc: Two monsters work for an energy firm that employs scary creatures to sneak into children's bedrooms and convert their screams into power. However, when a little girl accidentally wanders into the pair's domain, they have to race against time to return her safely home before anyone finds out. Animated comedy, with the voices of John Goodman, Billy Crystal, Steve Buscemi and James Coburn.

programme.title: The Haunted Mansion
programme.desc: Overworked estate agent Jim Evers takes his beleaguered family to look round an isolated, crumbling mansion - but the resident ghosts are not especially pleased to see the visitors. Comedy based on the Disney theme-park ride, starring Eddie Murphy, Terence Stamp, Jennifer Tilly and Marsha Thomason.

programme.title: Mufasa: The Lion King
programme.desc: Mufasa, a cub lost and alone, meets a sympathetic lion named Taka, the heir to a royal bloodline - a chance meeting which sets in motion an expansive journey of a group of misfits searching for their destiny. Prequel to Disney's live-action 2019 movie, with the voices of Aaron Pierre, Kelvin Harrison Jnr and Tiffany Boone.

programme.title: Beauty and the Beast
programme.desc: A prince is transformed into a hideous monster as punishment for his selfishness, and can only regain his human form by finding true love. Salvation comes in the form of a spirited village girl, who offers to take her father's place when he is imprisoned in the monster's castle. But as romance blossoms between the unlikely pair, a jealous rival suitor only sees a beast to be slain. Live-action remake of the Disney animated fairy tale, starring Emma Watson, Dan Stevens and Luke Evans, with Ewan McGregor, Emma Thompson and Ian McKellen playing the Beast's entourage of living ornaments.

programme.title: Iron Man
programme.desc: Arms manufacturer Tony Stark is taken hostage by a terrorist group and realises the weapons his company build have been falling into the wrong hands. Using his engineering skills to construct a hi-tech armoured suit, he manages to escape and then puts the technology to good use in the fight against evil around the world. Superhero adventure, starring Robert Downey Jr, Jeff Bridges, Gwyneth Paltrow and Terrence Howard.

programme.title: The Avengers
programme.desc: A mystical artefact is stolen from a top-secret military base by Thor's brother Loki, who plans to use it to bring about an alien invasion. Spymaster Nick Fury brings together a team of superheroes, including Iron Man, Thor, Captain America and the Hulk, to defend Earth from the impending attack. Action adventure uniting the Marvel comic-book characters, starring Robert Downey Jr, Chris Evans, Chris Hemsworth, Mark Ruffalo, Scarlett Johansson, Tom Hiddleston, Jeremy Renner and Samuel L Jackson.

programme.title: Alien: Romulus
programme.desc: While scavenging items from a derelict space station, a group of young colonisers fight for survival when they cross paths with lethal life forms. Co-writer/director Fede Alvarez's horror sequel set between the events of Alien and Aliens, starring Cailee Spaeny, David Jonsson and Isabela Merced.

programme.title: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
programme.desc: Four children are evacuated from London during the Second World War and sent to a rural manor house where they discover a secret entrance to the mystical world of Narnia. There they help vanquish the wicked White Witch, whose curse has gripped the land in perpetual winter. Fantasy adventure based on the book by CS Lewis, with Tilda Swinton, Georgie Henley, Skandar Keynes, Anna Popplewell, William Moseley, James McAvoy and Jim Broadbent, and featuring the voice of Liam Neeson.

programme.title: Myth: A Frozen Tale
programme.desc: A family sits down for a bedtime story and is transported to a forest filled with elemental spirits. Animated short.

programme.title: Ratatouille
programme.desc: A rat finds his love of fine food has made him an outcast to his less discerning family. Separated from his fellow rodents by a storm, he winds up in a famous French restaurant, where he helps an incompetent kitchen assistant become the greatest chef in Paris. Animated comedy from the director of The Incredibles, with the voices of Patton Oswalt, Ian Holm, Lou Romano and Peter O'Toole.

programme.title: A Bug's Life
programme.desc: Well-meaning ant Flick lands his colony in trouble when he accidentally disposes of an offering meant for a swarm of greedy grasshoppers - who promptly promise a horrible revenge. Faced with the imminent destruction of the anthill, he sets out to save the situation by enlisting the help of a few would-be heroes - an out-of-work troupe of bugs from a low-rent flea circus. Pixar animation, with the voices of Dave Foley, Kevin Spacey and Julia Louis-Dreyfus.

programme.title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Dog Days
programme.desc: Weedy youngster Greg finds his plans for a lazy school holiday ruined when his mother bans video games and his father organises a series of family activities. When he finds out a girl he likes is working at a country club, he tells his family he has a summer job there as an excuse to spend time with her - but struggles to keep up the deception. Family comedy sequel, starring Zachary Gordon and Steve Zahn.

programme.title: Cinderella
programme.desc: An orphan is forced to live a life of servitude by her cruel stepmother. The king of the realm she lives in organises a lavish ball to find a bride for his son, and a caring fairy godmother puts her magic to the task of turning the downtrodden girl into a princess. Animated fairytale, with the voices of Ilene Woods, William Phipps and Verna Felton.

programme.title: The Good Dinosaur
programme.desc: In a world where the asteroid impact that wiped out the dinosaurs never happened, humans have evolved as a primitive species while the giant lizards remain the dominant life form on Earth. A young apatosaurus becomes separated from his family, but finds a friend in a feral human boy as he makes the dangerous journey home. Pixar animated adventure, with the voices of Raymond Ochoa and Jack Bright.

programme.title: The Princess Diaries
programme.desc: An ordinary teenager discovers she is descended from royal stock and her grandmother is a queen. However, when this formidable regal lady insists she learn to behave like a princess, life suddenly becomes very complicated. Family comedy, starring Anne Hathaway, Julie Andrews, Heather Matarazzo and Hector Elizondo.

programme.title: Man v. Food Nation
programme.desc: S4 E18 — St. PaulAdam Richman's eating adventure has brought him to St Paul, Minnesota. First, Adam heads to Punch Pizza where he'll get to taste an authentic margherita pizza pie.

programme.title: Man v. Food Nation

programme.title: Man v. Food Nation

programme.title: Man v Food
programme.desc: S1 E4 — ColumbusAdam Richman faces another tough eating challenge in Columbus when he attempts to eat a two-and-a-half pound Dagwood Sandwich. Will he have enough room for dessert?

programme.title: Man v Food
programme.desc: S1 E1 — AmarilloAdam Richman visits Coyote Bluff in Amarillo, Texas, a joint known for a burger so spicy it's dubbed the Burger From Hell. He also encounters a killer steak at the Big Texan Steak Ranch.

programme.desc: S1 E4 — HoneyJames Martin uses honey to create dishes such as cod with honey onions, apple tart with honey and walnut ice cream and saffron and honey pears, then he dons a bee suit to enter a hive.

programme.title: James Martin Delicious
programme.desc: S1 E5 — AsparagusJames prepares asparagus tart, poached egg with asparagus, char grilled asparagus with red pepper and visits a local grower.

programme.title: James Martin Delicious
programme.desc: S1 E6 — SpanishTime for chick pea and spinach tapas, Andalusian pork, charred tuna romesco and Iberian ham salad. Then James pays a visit to Borough market in London to track down the best Spanish ingredients.

programme.title: James Martin Delicious
programme.desc: S1 E7 — CheeseJames Martin cooks cheese with roast figs and prosciutto, baked cheese in a box and a classic Greek salad. Then he visits Lyburn Farm to see how cheese is made.

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: S10 E3 — Bread WeekIt's Bread Week and the bakers tackle a signature bake designed to be shared. Then, the bakers must tackle a deceptively simple summer staple in the Technical and to finish there is an ambitious Showstopper.

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: S10 E4 — Dairy WeekIt's Dairy Week and Prue and Paul have set some tricky challenges including a Technical that dates back to Henry VIII and a Showstopper usually found at Indian weddings.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E11 — BirminghamJames visits the capital of the balti - Birmingham. Here he meets acclaimed food critic, broadcaster, columnist and author, Grace Dent. Swapping the mini for a narrow boat, James takes in the culture, which saw an industrial revolution. James's trip down the stretch of the 35-mile canal system inspires him to cook his version of a chicken balti. Grace explores the revolution of Birmingham and its food scene by starting at the famous Balti Triangle.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E12 — NottinghamJames travels to Nottingham, where he sets up his mobile kitchen in the middle of Sherwood Forest and cooks a Forest Pork Feast for long-time pal and Michelin award-winning restaurateur Sat Bains. James visits Keith Gascoigne, the inventor of a medal winning Para-Olympic bow. He learns the art of bow making, to practice for a surprise for Sat Bains. Feeling peckish, James cooks sausage rolls with crispy bacon, and a fruity dipping sauce.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The chefs must cook their fish courses but with some exceptionally high scoring dishes in the regional heats, each chef will need to deliver perfection in order to see off the competition. The judges are joined by guest judge Tim Henman.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is main course day and with only two spots remaining on the banquet menu, the competition is fierce. As the barbecues are fired up, all 8 chefs are feeling the heat. The judges are joined by guest judgeand Paralympic gold medallist, Gordon Reid.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is dessert day and with just one place remaining at the Wimbledon banquet, each chef is giving everything they have got. The judges are joined by guest judge Annabel Croft, former British Number One and Junior Wimbledon Champion.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the grand finale and the winning chefs must now cook their dishes at the banquet. Once in the kitchen, the chefs face the huge challenge of scaling up their dishes.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Competing for top spot are Danny Parker, head chef at Michelin starred `House of Tides' in Newcastle, who is back to try his luck in the competition again after being knocked out in the regional heat last year following a tense tie-break. He's taking on two newcomers: Dan Fletcher, protégé of Phil Howard, and now head chef at `Fenchurch' in the City of London, and David Coulson,who runs `Peace and Loaf' in Newcastle, which boasts 2 AA rosettes.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: After a tense starter course the chefs are all aiming for 10s with their unique fish dishes. David is celebrating a personal connection to the brief with his `My Cod I Bet Me Ma'am Has Seen Some Trotters', a tribute to his mum who has worked as a chiropodist. Dan's `For All Those Sleepless Nights' pays tribute to nightshift workers from the NHS with some bold but classic flavours while Danny's `Not All Superheroes Wear Capes' aims to give a taste of luxury to the hardworking staff.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Dan pays tribute to an icon of modern nursing, Florence Nightingale, while Danny in inspired by the founder of the NHS, Aneurin Bevan. David's dish is dedicated to the air ambulance staff who saved the life of his fiancé, and he even takes a trip to meet one of them.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the chefs' last chance to impress and tensions are high. Dan takes a risk with an unusual combination of ewe's milk and bergamot while Danny is determined to pull out all the stops with his complex dessert `Aunty Gwen's Chocolate'. David hopes to transform a childhood comfort classic into a show stopping dessert. Dan also takes a trip to meet Dr Ben Clarke who was working in the Royal London Hospital A&E during the London Bridge terror attack.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The two remaining North East chefs must cook their four course menus again, but will they take on board their veteran's advice as they serve their `Feast To Say Thank You'?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Banquet champion Selin Kiazim, a rising star of the London scene renowned for her Turkish Cypriot fusion flavours, is back hoping to join the elite group of chefs who have made it to the banquet twice. She is up against James Cochran who's worked at some of London's toughest kitchens including 2 Michelin starred `The Ledbury' and Scott Goss from `The Twenty Six' in Tunbridge Wells, renowned for his use of local Kent ingredients.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The chefs do battle for the fish course and the atmosphere in the kitchen is tense. Lobster is catch of the day for James whose dish is Caribbean-inspired. Scott is attempting to elevate a classic fish pie, dedicated to his mum who worked as a pharmacist in the NHS for 23 years. And Selin is taking a risk with a complex three-part fish dish featuring sardines, scallops and langoustines, as a nod to the purported health benefits of a Mediterranean diet.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Scott is showcasing rare breed Tamworth pork to say thank you to the rare breed of people who work for the NHS. Selin is serving a complex duck dish using ingredients from all around the world to honour `Our Global NHS'. And James is presenting five cuts of goat cooked in five different ways, for his bold dish `Under The Knife'.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Selin puts her own unique twist on tea and toast. James creates a decadent coconut parfait accompanied by mango puree filled doughnuts for his dessert `Tree of Life' inspired by the coconut palm tree, the NHS and both of their contributions to our health. Scott hopes his elevated gypsy tart `Honey Bee Good' will secure him a place in the final.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The two remaining London and the South East chefs must cook their four-course menus again, but will they take on board their veteran's advice as they re-make their `Feast To Say Thank You'?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Vying to be crowned champion of Scotland are three talented newcomers to the GBM kitchen. Lorna McNee is a former Scottish Chef of the Year and is renowned for her technical precision which she has gained from working her entire career at 2 Michelin-starred restaurant Andrew Fairlie at Gleneagles.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the fish course and the chefs are all out to impress. The heat is increased as all three serve their unique takes on lobster. Ross is hoping to snatch victory with his dish `Lobster Aid'. Lorna's `Live Well, Live Very Well' features only three elements, each of which she needs to deliver perfection.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Ross is hoping to impress with `Oh Deer It's Time For Your Penicillin', his tribute to Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming featuring an unusual yeast element as well as venison. Across the kitchen, Lorna, a former Game Chef of the Year, is also cooking venison in a bid to impress.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's dessert day and the last chance for the chefs to impress before one is sent home. Ross is attempting to elevate a comfort classic into a dish worthy of the banquet. Lorna's cooking a personal tribute to the NHS staff who have cared for her during treatment for a rare blood condition, using unusual yuzu and tonka bean flavours. Once again Ben is serving an experimental dish with his `Dance for the Greater Good' which includes a bees wax ice cream.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's judging day and the two remaining chefs must impress the panel of Oliver Peyton, Andi Oliver and Matthew Fort. Both chefs are gunning for success and are doing everything they can to deliver their menus to perfection.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Three chefs compete in the heat for the central region. Returner Ryan Simson-Trotman, who failed to reach the national finals last year, is originally from Nuneaton and opened his own restaurant Orwells in the Oxfordshire countryside with his partner Liam, who is also a contestant in the North West region.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the fish course and the chefs are pulling out all the stops. Marianne pays tribute to the `angels' in her local hospital who looked after her during a recent illness. Ryan's dish is a reference to the purported health benefits of fish high in omega 3 oils. While Sabrina is inspired by her aunt, a retired nurse who used to take in food to share with her fellow workers during her shifts.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The chefs cook their mains and following yesterday's results, tension is high. Both Marianne and Ryan are cooking muntjac in the hope of impressing the veteran judge, while Sabrina is making an ambitious technical take on a family feast.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: With one dish left to impress the veteran judge, the chefs cook their desserts. Marianne is looking to raise a smile with her `carry on' themed dessert, complete with surprise presentation. Sabrina hopes to make it through with an elevated take on jelly and ice cream while Ryan goes all out with his very sweet treat `A Spoonful of Sugar'.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The two remaining central region chefs do battle for a place in the national finals. They must impress the formidable panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton with their four course menus.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Andrew is attempting to pay tribute to NHS staff with his innovative take on a traditional healing recipe, `Mum's Flu Fighting Chicken Soup'. Jason's `A Tea From The Heart' is a play on a post-war remedy which harks back to the era when the NHS was formed. And Chris is hoping to impress with his dish inspired by a therapeutic hospital garden featuring foraged herbs from the Welsh valley where he lives including wild chervil, pickled pine buds and yarrow tips.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: After the starter results, the chefs return to the kitchen hoping for high scores with their fish dishes. Chris once again is using ingredients he has foraged from around his restaurant, while Jason hopes to impress with a spicy scallop dish and Andrew prepares a cod dish with 11 different elements.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The chefs are pulling out all the stops in a bid for big scores with their mains. All three dishes pay tribute to the founder of the NHS Aneurin Bevan, Chris's `Everything But The Squeal' is an ambitious pork sharing platter, while Jason's `For The Rich And The Poor' showcases lamb, and Andrew is hoping to impress with `Aneurin Bevan For Better Steak'.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the dessert course and the last opportunity for the chefs to impress. Chris is hoping to triumph with another dish which showcases the foraged ingredients available around his restaurant, while Jason attempts a technical feat in his dessert inspired by a childhood hospital stay and Andrew is inspired by a dish by his great grandmother used to cook. Which two will make it through to the judging chamber?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the Wales regional final as the two remaining chefs do everything they can to impress the judging panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. After tensions ran high in the week, the chefs are under pressure to deliver perfection. The judges are joined by Aneira Thomas, the first baby born on the NHS, who is named in tribute to the service's founder Aneurin Bevan and who went on to dedicate her life to the service. Who will win a place in the national finals?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the turn of three chefs representing the South West, including two who have competed before but meet in the kitchen this week for the very first time.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the fish course and with Tom renowned as a fish specialist all eyes are on him. He's cooking his take on a classic British fish supper in tribute to a charity which looks after the health of local fishermen. Jude is attempting a complex fusion dish featuring four different fish and an unusual X Ray themed presentation, while Olivia is paying tribute to the staff who looked after her during the birth of her first son with her take on curried monkfish.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the main course and two of the chefs are hoping duck will win the day. Tom is preparing a technically challenging duck dish steeped in NHS history while Jude is making a multi-element Chinese duck dish inspired by his mum. Olivia is hoping her dish, using two unusual cuts of beef, will score top points. Olivia also visits her local children's hospital, home of the second busiest paediatric A&E in the country.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: With just one more chance to impress their veteran judge, the chefs are all hoping to use their pastry skills to deliver technically complex desserts. Tom's cooking an `Invalid Fruit Tart' inspired by a 1950s recipe, while Jude is making six different apple elements for his `An Apple A Day'. Olivia is using stout in reference to an outdated old wives' tale which suggested the drink was a healthy source of iron during pregnancy.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's time for the two remaining chefs representing the South West to go head to head as they cook their menus again for the exacting panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. With a spot in the National Finals at stake, both are aiming for perfection as they bid for glory. The judges are joined by Barbara Childs, a Matron in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit at Great Ormond Street Hospital, who isn't afraid to speak her mind in the chamber.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Three chefs take to the kitchen in a bid to represent the North West in the national final. They include Ellis Barrie, from the award winning Marram Grass in Anglesey, Liam Simpson-Trotman, an accomplished pastry chef and co-owner of the 4 AA rosette Orwell's in Oxfordshire, and Craig Sherrington, who sharpened his skills working under top names including Eric Chavot and is now Chef Patron of Virginia House in Cumbria.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the fish course and the chefs are all gunning for tens. Craig pays tribute to a friend who has revolutionised hospital food in Morecambe Bay, while Liam is inspired by health advice his grandma gave him and Ellis is dedicating his dish to the staff who delivered his son Albert. With cod, mackerel, shrimp and cockles on the menu, which of the chefs will score highly?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Time for the chefs to cook their mains and the pressure is on. Craig is hoping to impress using two cuts of Dexter beef, while Liam prepares his take on a Bajan lamb stew and Ellis prepares four cuts of suckling pig. Liam meets his personal hero, Nola Ishmael OBE, who became the UK's first ever black Director of Nursing.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the dessert course and the last chance for the North West chefs to impress in a bid to make it through to the regional final. Liam is cooking `Not So Hot Toddy' in honour of a friend who works nightshifts in the NHS, while Ellis' `Worth Their Weight in Gold' is dedicated to the staff who saved his brother's life and Craig's dish `The Missed Celebration' pays tribute to his wife with an unusual Christmas concept.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The two highest scoring chefs from the week return to cook their menus again. Judging them are Matthew Fort, Oliver Peyton and Andi Oliver who are joined by Dr Jake Dunning MBE, an infectious disease specialist who has been recognised for his work during the West Africa Ebola epidemic.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Three chefs are doing battle to represent Northern Ireland. Tommy Heaney, Head Chef at the Great House Hotel in South Wales is taken on by Shauna Froydenlund, Chef Patron at Marcus Waring's two Michelin starred restaurant and James Devine, the 2017 National Chef of the Year.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: After a tense starter course, the chefs return to the kitchen to cook their fish dishes. James is making his elevated take on a fried chicken takeaway as a tribute to the NHS staff who care for his sister. Shauna is also taking inspiration from a personal connection with a tribute to staff from a facility in her hometown of Londonderry. Tommy is hoping to impress with a dish dedicated to the discovery of DNA.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: With two courses down it's time for the chefs to cook their main courses. It's the battle of beef with each using the same meat in their innovative creations. Tommy also meets the first baby ever born on the NHS.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's dessert course and the final chance for the chefs to impress. After such a tightly fought battle all week, each is hoping to deliver a technically perfect dessert. programme.title: Jason Atherton's Dubai Dishes

Jason is joined by Daniel Birk, his own executive chef in Dubai, who samples some cocktails before creating a delicious lobster and mango dish.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: S2 E4On the sweeping sands of Benone Strand in Co Derry, Dermot O'Leary rolls up his trousers and wades into the sea to harvest water for salt-making, learning the traditional process of creating sea salt over an open fire right on the beach. Travelling on to Coleraine, Dermot tries lobster fishing and visits LIR seafood restaurant, where the chefs champion a zero-waste approach to cooking.

programme.title: The Goonies
programme.desc: Adventure based on a story by Steven Spielberg, starring Sean Astin, Corey Feldman and Martha Plimpton. While clearing out an attic, a gang of boys known as the "Goonies" come across a map revealing the location of a long-lost galleon. But when they begin their search for the vessel, they find the evil Mama Fratelli standing in the way of a fantastic adventure.

programme.title: Ainsley's Fantastic Flavours
programme.desc: S3 E3Chef Ainsley Harriott rustles up recipes made to share, tempting dishes that will impress any guest and an absolute feast perfect for friends and family, featuring a Vietnamese-inspired starter and a sumptuous roasted porchetta. Comedians Eddie Kadi and Babatunde Aléshé show off their skills in the kitchen and Ainsley enjoys a picnic in the sun, Malta-style.

programme.title: James Martin's American Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E20 — New YorkThe chef ends his coast-to-coast exploration of the US in New York City. After a bite of pizza at a popular pizzeria in Greenwich Village, James cooks on one of the city's famous piers. New York has a wealth of French fine-dining restaurants, and the chef cannot wait to take a bite of the action. He chooses his favourite pair, Daniel, run by his old mate Daniel Boulud, and Le Bernadine, where Eric Ripart is in charge. At the end of the day, James cooks back on the pier as sunset approaches and he reminisces on his journey of more than 3,000 miles.

programme.title: The FBI Files

programme.title: The FBI Files

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: S5 E21 — Deadly InfluenceAmid the cocaine wars of early 1980s Miami, three dead bodies led a multi-agency tactical squad to suspect that a group of cops might be involved in illegal drug busts.

programme.title: Nightmare Next Door

programme.title: Calls From the Inside

programme.title: Calls From the Inside

Beginning the journey near his childhood home in Charnwood Forest, Leicestershire, he learns how a fossil discovery transformed scientists' understanding of the evolution of complex organisms, and in Newfoundland and Australia he reveals the earliest kinds of animal to exist on the planet. With the help of cutting-edge technology and visual effects, the programme brings the creatures to life, demonstrating how they survived

programme.title: David Attenborough's First Life
programme.desc: In the conclusion of the two-part documentary, the naturalist travels to Burgess Shale in Canada's Rocky Mountains, where he explores how evolution gained pace once creatures developed mouths and mobility. In Scotland, he reveals that one of the smallest fossils found holds the secret to how animals began surviving on dry land, and explains the bloom of life during the oxygen-rich Carboniferous period

programme.title: David Attenborough's Natural History Museum Alive
programme.desc: The broadcaster invites viewers to join him as he takes an after-hours stroll around one of his favourite places, the Natural History Museum. But this is no ordinary tour as some of the many exhibits spring to life as the veteran naturalist strolls along

programme.title: Aussie Snake Wranglers: Deadly Pursuit
programme.desc: Jess and Dan grab a smelly snake before Stu rescues one at university

programme.title: Aussie Snake Wranglers: Deadly Pursuit
programme.desc: Mick and Adele separate mating eastern browns, while Stu and Liv search a warehouse as danger mounts

programme.title: Land of the Far North
programme.desc: Life in the Arctic Circle, where the sun hardly sets in summer. Food is abundant, but animals and plants alike face great challenges such as sleep deprivation, pests and predators

programme.title: Land of the Far North
programme.desc: Cold and darkness dominate the Arctic Circle during winter, but nature copes astonishingly well. This documentary reveals how plants and animals survive these brutal conditions

programme.title: Rewilding
programme.desc: Documentary about the European bison, the continent's biggest terrestrial mammal, which was hunted to extinction but has been re-introduced thanks to rewilding

programme.title: Rewilding
programme.desc: A visit to Steinhuder Meer, a biodiversity hotspot in Germany, a combination of fenlands, alder march and dunes which create an amazing landscape

programme.title: Rewilding
programme.desc: Andalucia consists of extreme habitats once severely impacted by humans. Now, many previously near-extinct animals are reclaiming this unique land

programme.title: The Wild Wild East
programme.desc: The wildlife of the Maritime Provinces on Canada's eastern shore. The first edition visits Prince Edward Island to explore the family life of the red fox, sly creatures adept at living just on the fringes of society

programme.title: The Wild Wild East
programme.desc: Cameras take to the sky with a bald eagle, seeing how they raise families, hunt and forage for food, and compete for territory with another bird of prey, the osprey

programme.title: The Wild Wild East
programme.desc: The creatures following the ebb and flow of the tides, including sandpipers migrating from the Arctic to South America and seals making a home on Nova Scotia's rocky coastline

programme.title: Great Parks of Africa
programme.desc: Land meets sea in The Garden Route, a famous park and wildlife paradise that's home to the humpback whale, the blue duiker antelope and the endangered Knysna seahorse

programme.title: Monkey Life
programme.desc: Alison and baby orangutan Sibu enjoy a walk in the park, while primate care staff member Donna is in Spain to collect another rejected orangutan

programme.title: Monkey Life
programme.desc: Orangutan baby Kiwi makes the journey from Spain to Dorset and meets her new companion Sibu. There are concerns for ageing chimp Butch after a vet visit

programme.desc: Anna chases the Nomads out of her territory, then join Mia in her birthing den, before kicking back with the Mangrove Family as they pal around with stray dogs

programme.desc: E8The bloodiest months of the war are still ahead. A Soviet surge pushes German forces back to within 30 kilometres of the Polish Border. The siege at Leningrad is lifted after 900 days and Operation Overlord, D-Day, opens a second front in Europe.

programme.title: Soviet Storm
programme.desc: E3Soviet troops suffered huge casualties in Rzhev in 1941, causing the bloody battle to be grimly nicknamed the Meat-Grinder. This is a look at events from the Russian perspective.

programme.title: Soviet Storm
programme.desc: E4An attack on Soviet oil fields could have won the Germans the war, but massive resistance thwarted Hitler's dream.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E2Unusually, we look at the later, clipped wing version flown by Czech refugee pilots in the UK during WW2. We get close-up with a beautifully restored example, fly her and unearth long unseen test and operational footage.

programme.title: Combat Trains
programme.desc: E5Twenty-four-year-old Winston Churchill boarded an armoured train during the Boer War hoping for a newspaper scoop. He was captured, but became world famous after escaping.

programme.title: The Lost Women Spies
programme.desc: E1During WWII, the French Resistance seeks aid from SOE. Led by Vera Atkins, Odette Sansom and Noor Inayat Khan fight the Nazis, risking it all for victory.

programme.title: The Lost Women Spies
programme.desc: E2Vera enlists Violette Szabo and Yvonne Baseden. With circuits failing and Noor at risk, treachery allegations harm preparations for the Allied invasion.

programme.title: The Lost Women Spies
programme.desc: E3With Allied victories and the liberation of Paris following D-Day, Vera is in a race against time to locate her missing agents.

programme.title: The Lost Women Spies
programme.desc: E4Armed with evidence from Odette, Vera intensifies her search at Karlsruhe prison and Ravensbruck, facing hurdles to uncover crucial results in Germany.

programme.title: The Lost Women Spies
programme.desc: E5Vera finds out her agents' fate. Her beliefs about Noor are challenged. Suspicions lead Vera to hunt down a Nazi mastermind.

programme.title: The Lost Women Spies
programme.desc: E6Capture of a key Nazi uncovers shocking realities. Amid demands for accountability, as Vera and her team navigate murky waters to confront uncomfortable truths.

programme.title: Cracking The Code
programme.desc: E1Uncovering some of the world’s most famous encryptions. Revealing how they were decoded, the brilliant minds who cracked them and the mysteries they were hiding.

programme.title: Cracking The Code
programme.desc: E3The Japanese Super Code reveals the US efforts to crack Japan's unbreakable WWII code following the horror of the attack on Pearl Harbor.

programme.title: Cracking The Code
programme.desc: E6A look at America's Cold War codebreakers charged with unravelling a seemingly uncrackable Soviet code and the uncovering of the Manhattan Project.

programme.title: Cracking The Code
programme.desc: E7Revealing the encrypted German telegram could save Britain in its darkest hour. Can a team of geniuses decode the message in time?

programme.title: Soviet Storm
programme.desc: E8Stalin’s USSR was highly experienced in espionage. Yet Hitler’s invasion still caught the Soviets off-guard. Thereafter, though, the GRU and NKVD went on to score amazing intelligence coups in Tokyo, Washington and even the heart of Berlin.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E7The Battle of Leyte Gulf tells the story of the largest sea conflict in history involving Pearl Harbor warships and the largest battleships in the world, and how the US Navy, despite kamikaze attacks and a Japanese decoy fleet, were victorious.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E8In this episode we look at vessels built for amphibious combat. We begin by looking at the last reaming Landing Craft Tank (LCT) to serve on D-Day – LCT 7074. These huge landing craft were essential in delivering tanks, trucks, soldiers and supplies.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E3The definitive, if not the best, Axis fighter of World War two: we delve into the story of legendary ace Adolf Galland and examine in detail and example of the type in his colours. We also look at the technical heritage the 109 designers left.
